title: Dedicated fleet autoscaler: burst credits, throughput floor, and utilization telemetry
author: Jordan Kim
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets can experience transient hotspots where a slow reactive scale-up leads to brief but customer-visible throttling. Customers asked for a way to guarantee short-term throughput (burst) without permanently increasing reserved capacity. This PR implements a burst-credit system, a configurable throughput_floor for each fleet, and enhanced utilization telemetry to make autoscaler decisions auditable and to power billing/observability dashboards.

Design summary: 1) Burst credits: each fleet tracks a credit bucket (credits accrue with underutilization and are consumed when observed demand exceeds current capacity). Credits translate to temporary allowance for extra allocations (burst instances) that autoscaler may create without changing permanent reserved replicas. 2) Throughput floor: a per-fleet config that enforces a minimum tokens-per-second throughput guarantee; the autoscaler will attempt to keep effective capacity >= throughput_floor during business hours. 3) Telemetry: emit "fleet.burst_credit", "fleet.burst_used", "fleet.effective_throughput", and per-allocation utilization histograms. New telemetry labels include fleet_id, pool, allocation_tier. 4) Config schema: add autoscaler_v2.yaml with backward-compatible defaults (burst disabled by default). 5) Rollout: opt-in via fleet config; start canary on 3 dedicated clusters for 48 hours with strict SLOs and alerting.

Checklist: 
- [x] Burst credit algorithm implemented (scale_manager.go).
- [x] Throughput floor enforcement (allocation_planner.go).
- [x] Telemetry mappings and Prometheus metrics + OTLP exporter changes (telemetry/metrics_mapper.go).
- [x] End-to-end integration test harness (scripts/loadtest/scale_probe.py).
- [x] Docs: ops runbook and migration notes (docs/ops/dedicated-autoscaling.md).
- [x] Canaries and dashboard queries added to observability-pack.

Testing: unit tests for the credit math (includes edge cases for negative credits, overflow, and concurrent accrual). Integration test runs against local k8s cluster with synthetic traffic patterns (burst, plateau, ramp) show median scale-up latency reduced by ~30% under the same committed capacity. CI: full test matrix ran; an integration flake was rerun and then passed.

Linear: ENG-3421. Related: SRE-118 (alerting workstream).

Rollout notes: default is disabled; customers opt in by setting autoscaler.v2.enabled = true on fleet config. There is an emergency feature-flag to disable burst globally. When enabling, monitor metrics: fleet.burst_used > 0 and fleet.effective_throughput < throughput_floor -> investigate allocation churn or misconfigured floor.

release_notes: Added optional burst-credit autoscaling and throughput_floor guarantees for Dedicated fleets. Opt-in via autoscaler.v2.enabled. Includes telemetry for burst usage and effective throughput. Backward compatible; disabled by default.
review_comments: Priya Shah (2025-11-04): Can you clarify how credits are persisted across controller restarts? We should persist minimal state to Etcd to avoid a cold-start penalty.

Jordan Kim (2025-11-04): Credits are persisted as a compact counter in fleet state CRD; added a durable write with eventual consistency to avoid hot Etcd pressure. See scale_manager.go commit for details.
Liam O'Connor (2025-11-06): Suggest adding a safety limit to burst-enabled fleets to avoid cascading allocation explosions during region-wide incidents.
Jordan Kim (2025-11-06): Added max_burst_allocations config and a global feature-flag to disable burst during incidents. Also added conservative defaults in autoscaler_v2.yaml.
Elena Rodriguez (2025-11-07): Telemetry labels look good; add allocation_tier label so we can correlate CL and reserved allocations in dashboards.
Jordan Kim (2025-11-07): Added allocation_tier label and updated observability-pack dashboard queries.
rollback_instructions: Disable autoscaler.v2.enabled on affected fleets or set autoscaler.v2.burst.enabled=false via fleet config; for global rollback, flip feature-flag in config-service and restart controllers. Monitor fleet.effective_throughput and allocation churn after rollback.
notes: Performance impact: minor additional CPU on controller for credit accounting (~2-3% at peak).
Cost model: burst usage is tracked and will be surfaced in billing; initial phase will not auto-bill customers without consent.
Canary plan: enable on 3 clusters, run for 48 hours, monitor burst_used, allocation churn, and tail latency dashboards.
